question: True or false: in daily life, people high in self-control fight off temptations more often than other people do?
answer: False. When Hofmann and colleagues beeped 205 adults at random through a week, those high in self-control reported fewer temptations and fewer bouts of resisting them. Their edge seemed to lie upstream, in lives arranged so the fight came up less often: no biscuits in the cupboard, the gym bag packed by the door.
move: The easiest temptation to beat is the one arranged out of reach.
trap: Crediting their good record to winning more fights with temptation.
reference: Hofmann, Baumeister, Förster & Vohs, Everyday temptations: an experience sampling study of desire, conflict, and self-control, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2012
